claim: AoE2DE_s.exe is the controlled native runtime reference.
evidence: Installed executable metadata and SHA-256 verification.
consequence: All native evidence is build-scoped to this executable unless explicitly qualified otherwise. The local installation path is intentionally excluded from the public record.

claim: The AI layer consumes .ai/.per rule material.
evidence: Installed AI tree, stock source, load statements, AI Script vocabulary.
consequence: Source architecture must target the script rule substrate rather than an external controller.

claim: Player AI rule filenames are resolved/acquired by native scenario/game code.
evidence: Embedded getOrExtractPlayerAiRulesFileName vocabulary and aiRulesFileData/mAiScriptBaseName fields.
not_proven: Complete loader call sequence and ownership.

claim: Expert rules participate in TribeStrategyAIModule loading.
evidence: loadExpertRules symbol and TribeStrategyAIModule context.
not_proven: Exact lifecycle timing and relationship to player AI file loading.

claim: Native rule state contains rule IDs, priority, min/max intervals, and current/sorted rule indices.
evidence: mCurrentRuleID, mPriority, mMinInterval, mMaxInterval, mNextSortedRuleIndex, mRules, mSortedRules vocabulary and diagnostics.
consequence: Lexical source order cannot be assumed to equal execution order.

claim: Rules are represented in a sorted execution structure.
evidence: mSortedRules, mNextSortedRuleIndex, numberSortedRules, failed-to-sort diagnostics.
not_proven: Exact sort comparator and rebuild trigger.

claim: XS exposes dynamic rule and rule-group lifecycle controls.
evidence: xsEnableRule, xsDisableRule, xsDisableSelf, xsEnableRuleGroup, xsDisableRuleGroup, xsIsRuleGroupEnabled.
consequence: Lifecycle can be an explicit architectural primitive.

claim: XS exposes dynamic priority and interval controls.
evidence: xsSetRulePriority/Self, xsSetRuleMinInterval/Self, xsSetRuleMaxInterval/Self.
not_proven: Exact legal ranges and scheduling mathematics.

claim: Native scheduler validates duplicate and invalid rule metadata.
evidence: Errors 0265, 0267, 0270, 0277, 0280, 0314, 0315 plus invalid ID/range diagnostics.
consequence: Malformed scheduler state must be treated as a normal fault class.

claim: Rule groups are first-class native structures.
evidence: mRuleGroups, numberRuleGroups, group allocation/activation diagnostics, group XS APIs.

claim: Goals, strategic numbers, and timers form a distributed AI state substrate.
evidence: Script usage and UP vocabulary including set/modify/get goal/SN/timer operations.
consequence: AEGIS can represent persistent state without external memory.

claim: UP exposes broad fact/object/player/target/resource/map observations.
evidence: up-get-fact family, object/type/target data, player/focus facts, resource amount/percent, terrain/elevation/zone/distance APIs.
consequence: Observation layer can be materially richer than static thresholds.

claim: UP exposes engine feasibility predicates for build/research/train.
evidence: up-can-build, up-can-build-line, up-can-research, up-can-train.
consequence: Authority can gate commands on engine-visible feasibility.

claim: UP contains a stateful search/filter workflow.
evidence: up-reset-search, up-full-reset-search, up-reset-filters, up-filter-include/exclude/distance/range/status/garrison, up-find-local/remote/resource/player.
consequence: Search procedures should establish query context explicitly.

claim: UP group creation is bounded and fallible.
evidence: up-create-group diagnostics for control group, count, starting index, and empty local list.
consequence: Group allocation requires validation/recovery.

claim: Concrete unit IDs, unit-line IDs, and class IDs are semantically distinct.
evidence: Project validator/runtime investigation and unit-type-count semantics.
consequence: API ledgers must record identifier domain, not merely integer value.

claim: Argument ranges can depend on API context even when backed by the same underlying numeric state type.
evidence: temporary-goal 3500 storage use versus narrower comparison contexts.

claim: Native action state distinguishes order, action, target, result, completion, failure, invalidation, and search-required conditions.
evidence: Action diagnostics and state vocabulary from native AI interface investigation.
consequence: Command issuance cannot be treated as success.

claim: Native tactical execution can preserve, invalidate, or replace targets.
evidence: current-target, target-moved, target-dead, better-target, retargeting and pathability diagnostics.
consequence: Strategic target intent must be separated from tactical target management.

claim: Pathability and geometry can invalidate intended movement/attack behavior.
evidence: cannot-path diagnostics, distance, terrain, point and evasive movement vocabulary.
consequence: Authority must account for map execution constraints.

claim: Build/train actions and production feasibility are engine-mediated operations.
evidence: up-build, up-train, can-build/can-train, pending objects, train-site readiness vocabulary.
consequence: Production director should be capability- and queue-aware.

claim: Research has explicit status/cost interfaces.
evidence: up-research, up-research-status, cost vocabulary.
consequence: Technology should be represented as an investment with postcondition.

claim: The machine has multiple explicit fault boundaries.
evidence: parse/interpret diagnostics, scheduler failures, action failures, invalidation and path errors.
consequence: AEGIS needs fault taxonomy and recovery states.

claim: Recovered source archives did not yield direct clean definitions for several BXS rule objects.
evidence: Pass 21 direct-definition searches returned no source matches for BXSRuleModule/BXSRuleEntry/BXSRuleGroupEntry and related fields.
consequence: Do not fabricate interpreter source from names; use binary evidence and qualified source contracts.

claim: Naming-based searches for intuitive interpreter/scheduler functions are insufficient.
evidence: Pass 23 broad searches for UpdateAI/EvaluateRules/ExecuteRule/ScheduleRule/InterpretRule/InterpretTrigger and variants returned no direct source matches.
consequence: Function names alone are not a reliable recovery strategy.

claim: Recovered AGE/genieutils material contains useful adjacent source-contract evidence but cannot automatically be treated as shipped-runtime interpreter source.
evidence: Passes 9, 20, 21 and 24 show mixed editor/tool/source material, embedded build paths, and absent BXS definitions.
consequence: Provenance matching is mandatory.

claim: The shipped executable is PE32+ x64 with eight observed sections.
evidence: Pass 24 PE inspection: machine 0x8664, optional magic 0x020B, section count 8.
consequence: Reverse-engineering workflow must use x64 PE assumptions.

claim: Ghidra Pass 33 produced a real analysis workspace and active analysis state.
evidence: Fresh project import, active javaw process, growing memory/CPU, Pass33 logs.
not_proven: Every decompiler result is trustworthy; repair noise exists.
consequence: Use targeted function validation after broad analysis.

claim: Pass 33 broad analysis generated substantial function-body repair noise.
evidence: PASS33B log contained thousands of overlap repair messages and bad-body removals.
consequence: Do not equate successful analysis completion with semantic correctness.

claim: The strongest architecture is a closed-loop controller separating observation, belief, intent, authority, execution, verification, and memory.
evidence: Convergence of UP observation APIs, scheduler lifecycle, feasibility predicates, action result states, historical AI structure, and Porphyra experiments.
consequence: This is the AEGIS architectural north star, subject to future evidence amendments.
